items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: And Art Hickman, I think, was one of the first bands, if not the first dance band, that Columbia imported. And we had a terrific time recording it with both saxophones.

ctx.x: Now, it wasn't just the novelty of the counterpoint and the conglomerate sound.

Well, oh, yeah, I think musically, I think musically, too, the band hit. It was something new and something that had a terrific lift, a beat as we call it now, and it, there it was. Before that, we at Columbia were using Prince's Band, making these 12-inch records of medleys, of tunes, which were supervised by the Hepburn Dance School at the time, to make sure that they got the proper one-step and two-step, not two-step, but foxtrot tempos, for which the records were sold, strictly for dancing. But it was not…
We mentioned that Earl Fuller worked for you for a time. How long were you with Columbia?
